title: Grateful Dead Live at Providence Civic Center on 1973-09-15
lineage: set 1: AUD> M?> C> C> D> SHN; set 2: SBD> MR> D> CD> EAC>SHN

ai_review.summary: Horns‑filled second set shines with crisp soundboard mix, while the audience‑recorded first set sounds muddy.
ai_review.review: The show is celebrated for its September ’73 horn experiment – the second set (starting with Mississippi Half‑Step) delivers standout performances of “Eyes of the World,” the Weather Report Suite, “Truckin’” and “Bird Song,” all captured on a clean soundboard feed. The first set suffers from typical 70’s audience tape quality, which some listeners find rough, but the musical firepower of the band more than makes up for it.

ai_rating.rationale: Average reviewer rating is 4.55/5; most praise the musical performance (especially the second set) and the soundboard portion, while noting only modest issues with the audience‑recorded first half.

recording_quality.technical_notes: First set is a typical 70's audience composite – muddy, uneven levels and occasional roughness. Second set is sourced from the soundboard (SBD) and is warm, clear and well‑balanced.

show_quality.setlist_flow: The second set opens with Mississippi Half‑Step and flows into a horn‑enhanced jam sequence; the horns add color without disrupting the band’s tight playing, creating a memorable, energetic arc.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s guitar is repeatedly praised – “on fire,” “flame flying,” and “mind‑bending beauty.”
band_member_comments.Phil: Mix notes mention Phil’s bass sounding a bit light in the first set, likely due to the audience tape.
band_member_comments.Keys: One reviewer wonders if Keith (the keyboardist) took lead vocals on “Let Me Sing Your Blues Away,” suggesting his presence on vocals.
